arxiv-1505-02458.title: Saturation and Geometrical Scaling: from Deep Inelastic ep Scattering to Heavy Ion Collisions Thanks: Presented at the Conference Excited QCD , Taranska Lomnica, Slovakia, March 8 – 14, 2015.
arxiv-1505-02458.creator: Michal Praszalowicz
arxiv-1505-02458.description: Abstract Saturation of gluon distribution is a consequence of the non-linear evolution equations of QCD. Saturation implies the existence of so called saturation momentum which is defined as a gluon density per unit rapidity per transverse area. At large energies for certain kinematical domains saturation momentum is the only scale for physical processes.

arxiv-2102-11364.title: Bimodules and matched pairs of noncommutative BiHom-(pre)-Poisson algebras
arxiv-2102-11364.creator: Ismail Laraiedh
arxiv-2102-11364.description: Abstract The purpose of this paper is to introduce the notion of noncommutative BiHom-pre-Poisson algebra. Also we establish the bimodules and matched pairs of noncommutative BiHom-(pre)-Poisson algebras and related relevant properties are also given. Finally, we exploit the notion of 𝒪 \mathcal{O} -operator to illustrate the relations existing between noncommutative BiHom-Poisson and noncommutative BiHom pre-Poisson algebras.

arxiv-2105-02077.title: Identification of causal effects in case-control studies
arxiv-2105-02077.creator: *, Rolf H.H. Groenwold
arxiv-2105-02077.description: Abstract Case-control designs are an important tool in contrasting the effects of well-defined treatments. In this paper, we reconsider classical concepts, assumptions and principles and explore when the results of case-control studies can be endowed a causal interpretation. Our focus is on identification of target causal quantities, or estimands.

arxiv-2106-07976.title: Federated Learning for Internet of Things: A Federated Learning Framework for On-device Anomaly Data Detection
arxiv-2106-07976.creator: Tuo Zhang*, Chaoyang He*, Tianhao Ma, Lei Gao, Mark Ma, Salman Avestimehr
arxiv-2106-07976.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tuo Zhang*, Chaoyang He*, Tianhao Ma, Lei Gao, Mark Ma, Salman Avestimehr. Federated learning can be a promising solution for enabling IoT cybersecurity (i.e., anomaly detection in the IoT environment) while preserving data privacy and mitigating the high communication/storage overhead (e.g., high-frequency data from time-series sensors) of centralized over-the-cloud approaches.

arxiv-2207-03440.title: The isovector axial form factor of the nucleon from lattice QCD
arxiv-2207-03440.creator: Dalibor Djukanovic, Georg von Hippel, Jonna Koponen, Harvey B. Meyer, Konstantin Ottnad, Tobias Schulz, Hartmut Wittig
arxiv-2207-03440.description: Abstract The isovector axial form factor of the nucleon plays a key role in interpreting data from long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. We perform a lattice-QCD based calculation of this form factor, introducing a new method to directly extract its z z -expansion from lattice correlators. Our final parametrization of the form factor, which extends up to spacelike virtualities of 0.

arxiv-2210-01943.title: The dichotomy spectrum approach for a global nonuniform asymptotic stability problem: Triangular case via uniformization Thanks: The first author was funded by FONDECYT Regular Grant 1200653. The second author was funded by FONDECYT POSTDOCTORAL Grant 3210132. The third author was funded by FONDECYT
arxiv-2210-01943.creator: Álvaro Castañeda, Ignacio Huerta, Gonzalo Robledo
arxiv-2210-01943.description: Abstract . By considering the nonuniform exponential dichotomy spectrum, we introduce a global asymptotic nonuniform stability conjecture for nonautonomous differential systems, whose restriction to the autonomous case is related to the classical Markus–Yamabe Conjecture: we prove that the conjecture is verified for a family of triangular systems of nonautonomous differential equations satisfying boundedness assumptions.

arxiv-2304-05628.title: Bounding the Lagrangian Hofer metric via barcodes Thanks: The author was partially supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation (grant number 200021_204107)
arxiv-2304-05628.creator: Patricia Dietzsch
arxiv-2304-05628.description: Abstract . We provide an upper bound on the Lagrangian Hofer distance between equators in the cylinder in terms of the barcode of persistent Floer homology. The bound consists of a weighted sum of the lengths of the finite bars and the spectral distance. 1. Introduction and main results Let (M,\omega=-\mathrm{d}\lambda) be an exact symplectic manifold.

arxiv-2309-09126.title: HOW MUCH CAN ChatGPT REALLY HELP COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGISTS IN PROGRAMMING?
arxiv-2309-09126.creator: Chowdhury Rafeed Rahman, Limsoon Wong
arxiv-2309-09126.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chowdhury Rafeed Rahman, Limsoon Wong. ChatGPT, a recently developed product by openAI, is successfully leaving its mark as a multi-purpose natural language based chatbot. In this paper, we are more interested in analyzing its potential in the field of computational biology. A major share of work done by computational biologists these days involve coding up bioinformatics algorithms, analyzing data, creating pipelining scripts and even machine learning modeling and feature extraction.

arxiv-2402-06178.title: MusicMagus: Zero-Shot Text-to-Music Editing via Diffusion Models
arxiv-2402-06178.creator: Yixiao Zhang, Yukara Ikemiya, Gus Xia, Naoki Murata, Marco A. Martínez-Ramírez, Wei-Hsiang Liao, Yuki Mitsufuji, Simon Dixon
arxiv-2402-06178.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yixiao Zhang, Yukara Ikemiya, Gus Xia, Naoki Murata, Marco A. Martínez-Ramírez, Wei-Hsiang Liao, Yuki Mitsufuji, Simon Dixon. Recent advances in text-to-music generation models have opened new avenues in musical creativity. However, music generation usually involves iterative refinements, and how to edit the generated music remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach to the editing of music generated by such models, enabling the modification of specific attributes, such as genre, mood and instrument, while maintaining other aspects unchanged.

arxiv-2408-00185.title: Anharmonic quantum muon effects in the kagome antiferromagnet Zn-Barlowite
arxiv-2408-00185.creator: F. Hotz 1∗ , M. Gomilšek 2,3∗ , T. Arh 2,3 , A. Zorko 2,3 and H. Luetkens 1
arxiv-2408-00185.description: Abstract Muon spin spectroscopy ( μ \mu SR) is a powerful local probe technique e.g. used for the investigation of exotic frustrated magnetism. Ab initio simulations using Density Functional Theory with the muon treated as a point-like defect (DFT+ μ \mu ) are commonly employed to determine the interstitial lattice positions where the muon comes to rest after implantation.

arxiv-2602-06864.title: SURE: S afe U ncertainty-Aware R obot- E nvironment Interaction using Trajectory Optimization
arxiv-2602-06864.creator: Author Names Omitted for Anonymous Review. Paper-ID [580], Zhuocheng Zhang 1 , Haizhou Zhao 1 2 , Xudong Sun 1 , Aaron M. Johnson 1 3 , Majid Khadiv 1
arxiv-2602-06864.description: Abstract Robotic tasks involving contact interactions pose significant challenges for trajectory optimization due to discontinuous dynamics. Conventional formulations typically assume deterministic contact events, which limit robustness and adaptability in real-world settings. In this work, we propose SURE, a robust trajectory optimization framework that explicitly accounts for contact timing uncertainty.

pmc-11440805.creator: Qirui Guo, Dawei Liu, Xiaoting Wang, Chinese Critical Ultrasound Study Group (CCUSG)
pmc-11440805.description: Septic shock is a frequent critical clinical condition and a leading cause of death in critically ill individuals. However, it is challenging to identify affected patients early. In this article, we discuss new perspectives on the methods and uses of peripheral perfusion monitoring, considering the concept of a dysregulated response.

pmc-13566783.title: Group 3 Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Insights, Clinical Challenges, and Evolving Therapies
pmc-13566783.creator: Steven C. Liu, Madeline Ku, Priyanka Mohnani, Tanvi Borse, Bharat Bajantri
pmc-13566783.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Group 3 pulmonary hypertension is a common and clinically significant complication of chronic lung disease and hypoxia that is associated with impaired functional capacity, right ventricular dysfunction, and increased mortality. Historically viewed as a consequence of underlying parenchymal lung disease, Group 3 pulmonary hypertension is now recognized as a complex disorder involving pulmonary vascular remodeling, dysregulated molecular signaling, and maladaptive cardiopulmonary interactions.

pmc-13644438.title: Routine health examination indicators for fatty liver disease risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction: a cross-sectional study of 46,311 individuals
pmc-13644438.creator: Chaochao Wang, Huiting Rao, Xuefei Zhang, Guibiao Zhang, Guodong Xia, Li Zhang
pmc-13644438.description: BackgroundFatty liver disease is frequently identified during routine health examinations, but practical strategies for risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction remain limited. This study evaluated metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) prevalence across thyroid function categories and developed health examination–based risk stratification models.

pmc-13700284.title: Comparative genomics of Begonia chloroplasts: insights into molecular evolution, species identification, and phylogeny
pmc-13700284.creator: Yang Huang, Wenxiu Tang, Secai Huang, Chao Xiong, Lan Wu
pmc-13700284.description: BackgroundBegonia, a hyperdiverse genus with ecological and medicinal values, confronts challenges in species identification and phylogenetic resolution due to remarkable morphological plasticity and ambiguous taxonomic boundaries. Chloroplast genomes (plastomes) serve as powerful molecular tools for addressing these issues, yet comprehensive plastomic data for Chinese Begonia species remain insufficient.
